_comment: The regions Kamome's self-hosted routing and map tiles cover.
Single source of truth for both halves of the stack: Deploy/bin/build-osrm.sh
merges these into ONE routing dataset (matching.base_url is a single value —
the app cannot pick a server per trip), and Deploy/bin/build-tiles.sh builds
ONE .pmtiles per region (a tile file covers a bounded area, and the app picks
the region covering each trip by reading its header).
Adding a region is an edit here, not a change to any script.
bbox is W,S,E,N in degrees, or null for the whole Geofabrik extract. Clip when
the extract is far larger than anywhere you actually travelled: it cuts
osrm-extract's peak RAM and the disk the .osrm.* files take, which is what
decides whether this builds on a laptop at all.
Tile bounds must COVER a trip or the app falls back to Apple's map, so leave
padding. Verify a built region with Tools/pmtiles-bounds.sh before side-loading.

regions.name: iceland
regions.note: Island + establishing headroom (2026-08-08). Was null = whole extract: a 518 km-tall region that pinned establishing and body to the same 291.5 km span. Sized per _establishing_headroom against the ring road's 491 km fitting span: containedSpan >= 1.5 x 491 = 737 km, so 1310 km of latitude and 737 km of longitude. All added area is open sea; 158.7 MB -> 159.5 MB.

regions.name: new-zealand
regions.note: North + South Island. Clipped because the Geofabrik extract also carries the Chatham Islands (-176°) and the Kermadecs, which straddle the antimeridian — unclipped, the built tiles declare bounds of -180…180 and the region claims to cover half the planet. Selection still works (latitude saves it), but the declared extent means nothing and the file is bigger for territory no trip will visit. Headroom already satisfied (2026-08-08): containedSpan 845 km against a 340 km fitting span is 2.48x, well over the 1.5x floor. Untouched.

regions.name: finland
regions.note: Whole country (703 MB) — the largest source here, and the first to clip if the merge is too heavy.

regions.name: miyakojima
regions.note: Geofabrik files Okinawa under kyushu (294 MB); the Miyako islands are a rounding error of it. Widened 2026-08-09 for establishing headroom — the old 125.10,24.60,125.55,25.00 clip supported trips only 17 km across against this trip's 32.4 km fitting span, so the film would have opened flat exactly as Iceland's did. Now containedSpan 48 km, rendering 47.2 -> 18.9 km = 2.50x. The margin is open sea: 1.2 MB either way. Still covers Miyako, Irabu, Shimoji, Kurima and Ikema.

_establishing_headroom.summary: containedSpan(region) >= wide_span_padding x fittingSpan(trip), or the opening has nothing to zoom out to.
why: Covering the trip is not enough. CameraPath.cappedToRegion refuses to frame
ground the tiles cannot draw, and that cap lands on the establishing beat and
the body span alike. Iceland shipped with a region 518 km tall: both pinned to
291.5 km, so the 'closing zoom' had no zoom in it (Docs/decisions.md 2026-08-08).
The requirement is simply that the region can hold the establishing beat:
containedSpan(region) >= fittingSpan(trip) x export.wide_span_padding  (1.5)
containedSpan is the widest PORTRAIT frame fitting inside the region, so for a
wide region it is bounded by latitude: 0.5625 x latExtent (0.5625 = 1080/1920).
In latitude that is 1.5 / 0.5625 = 2.67 x fittingSpan(trip).
HISTORY, because it cost two builds. This was briefly 1.875x. While the body
span also used wide_span_padding, the establishing beat and the body were the
same expression and collapsed into one another, so the only zoom available came
from a third, wider 'country' beat — which had to beat the regional beat by
opening_collapse_zoom_ratio, hence 1.25 x 1.5. Iceland was rebuilt to 1637 km of
latitude to satisfy that, and got a shallow 1.25x zoom sitting exactly on the
collapse threshold. Splitting body_span_padding out of wide_span_padding
(2026-08-08, Chiu, from renders) removed the need: the zoom now comes from
regional -> body directly, the country beat is unnecessary, and the region can
be smaller AND the zoom deeper (2.5x). If body_span_padding ever returns to
>= wide_span_padding, this requirement goes back to 1.875x.
cost: Cheap while the margin falls on water: empty tiles dedupe in PMTiles.
Iceland 158.7 MB -> 159.5 MB (+0.5%) for 518 km -> 1322 km of latitude.
(Measured with `ls`. An earlier note said +11%; that mixed `du` disk blocks
with `ls` bytes. The abandoned 1.875x build was 160.2 MB, +0.9%.)
A margin falling on LAND is different in kind, and not just for size: the
Geofabrik extract stops at the country, so a neighbouring landmass inside the
bounds has no OSM data and renders as OCEAN. Iceland's margin is open sea, so
this does not bite here — check it before widening a continental region.
